subject: Deployment options for QuickPay: bursty latency & throughput clarification
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@fastsend.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuickPay: post-demo details – burst profile and latencies

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — that was helpful. A few follow-ups from my side as we dig into feasibility:

- Traffic shape: we see steady background of ~400 req/s with 10–12x microbursts that last 20–60s during peak checkout flows (roughly 6–8 times per hour). Attached is a small sample (sample_traffic.csv).
- Latency targets: p50 < 40ms, p95 target <= 180ms for our user-facing checkout path. For async backfills p95 can be up to ~800ms.
- Data residency: US multi-region is a must.
- Go-live timeline: end of Q3 but we’d like a pilot in a 2–3 week window to validate SLOs.

High-level ask: we want guidance on which deployment mode makes sense (Hosted API initially to move fast vs Dedicated capacity for predictable SLAs), and ballpark cost/lead-time for Dedicated if that’s recommended.

—Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, FastSend
samir@fastsend.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fastsend.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@quickpay.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuickPay: post-demo details – burst profile and latencies

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the sample. Quick read: the burstiness and the tight p50/p95 targets for checkout point toward Dedicated capacity as the more predictable path if you need hard SLOs during traffic spikes. A few quick notes: 

- Hosted API: fastest to start (self-serve) and good for early validation. However, for 10–12x microbursts, we can see variable latency depending on shared capacity and cold-starts for certain kernels; tail behavior can be inconsistent.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools give consistent tail behavior (we can size based on your peak burst QPS and target concurrency). Autoscaling and burst pools can be configured but commit + lead time needed (typically 2–4 weeks to provision and calibrate).
- Private/VPC: unnecessary at this stage unless policy/compliance requires on-prem or VPC isolation.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Ben and I run a quick throughput/latency bench using your sample_traffic.csv (can simulate microbursts).
2) We propose two pilot configs: Hosted pilot (no commit) and Dedicated pilot (3–6 week reserved pool with canary routing). I’ll attach a draft MAP (mutual action plan) and a pilot config zip.

Questions for you: can you share peak concurrent user counts for checkout sessions and whether you expect heavy sequence lengths (long chat/history) on these calls? Also confirm preferred US regions (west/east).

I’m looping Ben to own the bench.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0197

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@quickpay.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>, Samir Shah <samir@fastsend.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuickPay: post-demo details — burst profile and latencies

Thanks Vivek — and Samir, adding a couple clarifications from our side: 

- Peak concurrent checkout sessions: ~1,200 active checkouts at peak (roughly maps to the bursts in the CSV).
- Payloads: short JSON payloads (~200–400 tokens equivalent); no long-context generation.
- Compliance: we prefer US-east for primary but can accept multi-region failover (east primary, west for DR).

Cost/lead time question: can you provide a ballpark of the 95th-percentile per-token cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated assuming our burst profile? Also curious about how Redwood’s autoscaling handles sustained bursts vs microbursts — will Dedicated always add capacity in discrete steps that could screw p95?

On attachments: I’ve uploaded an expanded traffic sample to the Drive link Vivek referenced.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Engineering Lead, QuickPay
priya.desai@quickpay.io
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@quickpay.io>, Samir Shah <samir@fastsend.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuickPay: post-demo details — burst profile and latencies

Priya/Samir — appreciate the extra detail. Quick operational plan and agreed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

1) Bench run (this week): Ben will run an offline bench using sample_traffic.csv to simulate 12x microbursts and report p50/p95 for Hosted vs a small Dedicated pool. Deliverable: bench results doc and recommended Dedicated sizing. (Owner: Ben; ETA: 72 hours)

2) Pilot options:
   - Hosted pilot: immediate, no commit, run 1 week of real traffic with passive telemetry for tail behavior. Good for early signal but not SLA-backed.
   - Dedicated pilot: 4-week reserved pool sized for observed burst peak with canary routing. Requires 2–3 week provisioning/calibration window. Recommended if you need enforceable SLOs for checkout.

3) Cost delta: we’ll include a cost sketch in Ben’s bench output (typically dedicated unit economics are better at sustained high throughput but have up-front commit). We’ll show per-100k request cost for your pattern.

4) Compliance/regions: We’ll size the Dedicated pool in us-east as primary and show failover options (us-west) — no private/VPC until you ask.

Action items:
- Samir/Priya: confirm you’re OK with a two-track pilot (Hosted quick-check + Dedicated sizing) and grant Ben access to the traffic sample in Drive.
- Ben: start bench and drop results + attachments to the Drive folder and HubSpot deal.
- Lauren: I’ve looped you for pricing/commit guidance and to prepare a draft pilot MSA if QuickPay prefers Dedicated after bench.

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min sync post-bench to review sizing and cost.

Thanks — Vivek
